newsitem.title: USA: NYSEG, Central Maine set gas plan.
newsitem.headline: NYSEG, Central Maine set gas plan.

text.p: New York State Electric & Gas Corp said Monday it signed a memorandum of understanding with Central Maine Power Co that could lead to the formation of a new natural gas distribution company to serve Maine customers.
The memorandum, signed last week, affirms the companies' intention to establish a framework for a jointly-owned company within six months, NYSEG said in a statement.

Central Maine has already asked the Maine Public Utilities Commission for permission to offer natural gas distribution service to Maine customers in areas not currently served by a natural gas utility, NYSEG said.
That could include areas like Augusta, Bangor, Brunswick, Rumford and Waterville. The Portland and Lewiston metro areas are already served by Northern Utilities Inc, a Bay State Gas Co subsidiary.
Various regulatory approvals would be required before Central Maine or a jointly-owned company could operate a new gas distribution service, NYSEG noted.

NYSEG Executive Vice President Michael German called the proposal "a logical extension of our natural gas business. Our expansion expertise and similarities with the CMP's service area regarding demographics, geography, customer mix and climate make this a perfect fit."
The opportunity for new retail distribution of natural gas depends on completion of either or both of two new pipeline proposals made by other organizations.

Maritimes & Northeast Pipeline LLC would run a natural gas transmission line from the Sable Island fields off Nova Scotia, while the Portland Natural Gas Transmission System would carry natural gas from western Canada through new or expanded pipelines extending through New Hampshire and Maine into Massachusetts.
Both projects are currently under federal and state regulatory review, while Canadian review of the Maritimes system has started.
"With the new pipelines proposed for Maine, we would hope to be able to serve new natural gas customers by 1999," said Central Maine President David Flanagan.
The Maritimes system is being proposed by Mobil Corp, Westcoast Energy Inc and PanEnergy Corp, which was acquired acquired by Duke Energy Corp in June.

Bay State Gas is the lead company in the Portland Natural proposal. Its partners are Gaz Metropolitain & Co LP, TransCanada PipeLines Ltd, MCN Energy Group Inc and U.S. Generating Co, a PG&E Corp affiliate.
